item.text: {"search_note":"I found no strong 2024 evidence that Abiy’s government made a durable nationwide move toward protecting digital freedom. The only positive item is the July 2024 restoration of connectivity in Amhara, which looks like partial de-escalation after a prolonged shutdown, not a rights-respecting reversal of the broader pattern.","evidence":[{"title":"Freedom on the Net 2024: Ethiopia","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/ethiopia/freedom-net/2024","summary":"Freedom House says authorities restricted mobile internet in Amhara, disrupted mobile internet during fighting, restricted social media in early February after protests in Oromia, and used the state of emergency to curtail online expression and detain journalists without charge. This is strong evidence for digital controls and shutdowns used to limit political freedom.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.6","4B.5"]},{"title":"World Report 2024: Ethiopia","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-01-12","url":"https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/ethiopia","summary":"HRW reports that the federal government tightly controlled reporting, detained critical voices, and repeatedly restricted internet and social media access; it also says journalists and opposition figures were arrested under emergency powers. This is direct evidence of administrative harassment and digital control.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.6","4B.5","4B.7"]},{"title":"Ethiopia: Authorities must stop using state of emergency law to silence peaceful dissent","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-02-19","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/ethiopia-authorities-must-stop-using-state-of-emergency-law-to-silence-peaceful-dissent/","summary":"Amnesty says the state of emergency was used to silence dissent through warrantless arrests, movement limits, bans on assemblies, and arrests of politicians and journalists, while also noting the extension was not transparently published. This is strong evidence of administrative harassment and information-control tactics.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.6","4B.5"]},{"title":"Ethiopia: Journalist arrested under state of emergency: Belay Manaye","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-03-14","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/afr25/7782/2024/en/","summary":"Amnesty reports Belay Manaye was arrested by police and security personnel, held without being told the reason, and believed detained for reporting on the Amhara conflict; it also says other journalists were arrested under the emergency. This is direct evidence of pressure on journalists and reprisals for reporting.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.6","4B.5"]},{"title":"Ethiopia: Internet services restored in Amhara region after 11-month blackout","publisher":"Internet Society Pulse","date":"2024-07-14","url":"https://pulse.internetsociety.org/en/shutdowns/internet-shutdown-in-amhara-region-ethiopia-august-2023/","summary":"The shutdown tracker says Amhara’s mobile internet, fixed-line internet, and platform restrictions were eventually restored in 19 cities by mid-July 2024 after an 11-month blackout. This is weak positive evidence only in the sense that one major shutdown ended; it does not show a general pro-freedom policy.","question_ids":["4B.9"]},{"title":"Ethiopia: End the month-long arbitrary detention of thousands in Amhara Region","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-11-06","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/ethiopia-end-the-month-long-arbitrary-detention-of-thousands-in-amhara-region/","summary":"Amnesty says a federal-regional task force used mass detention camps to silence peaceful dissent, describing arbitrary detention as a routine political tool under sweeping emergency laws. This supports a broader pattern of administrative harassment and coercive political control.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.5","4B.6","4B.7"]}]}
